lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The chamber where the threshold used to be. The walls are just walls now — stone and moss and the slow work of water finding its way down.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.monologue: I put my hand on the stone. It's cold. Just cold. There's no hum underneath, no sense of something vast pressing against the other side. It's a wall. It does what walls do.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.monologue: I wait for something. I don't know what. A flicker. A memory surfacing. The feeling I used to get — like standing at the edge of a cliff, except the cliff was in every direction and I was the edge.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.monologue: Nothing. Just stone under my palm and moss under my fingers and the sound of dripping water counting out seconds that belong to me now.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.monologue: I smile. It surprises me. Not the smiling — I do that now, more than I used to — but the reason for it. I thought I'd feel loss here. I thought I'd stand in this place and grieve for the vastness I gave up. The knowing. The being-between.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.monologue: Instead I feel the cold of the stone. And that's enough. Cold is specific. Cold is here. Cold is something that happens to a body that chose to have nerve endings.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.monologue: She's standing in the doorway. Of course she is. She followed me. She didn't say she would. She just appeared, the way she does — like she'd always been standing there and I just hadn't looked.

choices.text: I miss the knowing. But I'd rather choose.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.lens: His pulse is steady. His weight is balanced. He's not leaning toward the wall or away from it. He's just standing near a wall.
lines.monologue: He's telling the truth. I don't know why that makes my chest tight.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: I thought I would. I came here to see if I would. But it's just a wall.
lines.monologue: And I'm just a person standing next to it. That's the whole story.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.monologue: I don't say the rest. That I was afraid he'd touch the wall and disappear. That I walked an hour behind him ready to grab his arm. That 'good' is the largest word I can manage right now.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: I'm hungry. Is that a problem for all of us?
lines.monologue: She almost laughs. Almost. Her mouth does something that isn't quite a smile but is close enough.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: I miss the knowing. When I was between, I could feel everything at once. Every threshold, every edge, every place where one thing became another. It was like seeing the whole map instead of one road.
lines.monologue: That's true. He holds it carefully, the way you hold a glass thing that's already broken — not to fix it, just to look at the shape of it.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.monologue: To eat bread. To sleep badly. To not know what's coming next. To have hands that get cold.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.lens: His hand is on the wall. His other hand is at his side. Open. Not reaching for anything. Just available.
lines.monologue: I take his hand. The open one. I don't say anything. There's nothing to say that my hand isn't already saying.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.monologue: Her hand is warm. That's specific. That's here. That's what choosing feels like.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.monologue: I said 'home' without thinking. It's not a place. It's a camp with too many people and not enough chairs. But I said it and I meant it.
